📖 Core Definitions

Essential Terminology & Concepts

The Relation Core Definition

The Relation partial order because, some pairs of elements of domain under a partial order may not be related.

Relation Key Concept

The concept of 'relation' is one of the few fundamental concepts of mathematics.

Definition, Notation And Illustrations Key Concept

In Mathematics, a relation from a set X to a set Y is defined as a subset of the cross- product X xY.

Properties Of Relations Key Concept

We will discuss properties of only for those relations R for which the domain and range is the same set, say X, i.e., the relations on a set, say X.

Set-Type Operations On Relations Key Concept

The set-type operations on relations include union of relations, intersection of relations etc.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

2.2 Relation

  • The concept of 'relation' is one of the few fundamental concepts of mathematics.
  • We begin the discussion with its formal/ mathematical definition and illustrations through some well-known examples.
  • Definition, Notation and Illustrations In Mathematics, a relation from a set X to a set Y is defined as a subset of the cross- product X xY.
  • Earlier mentioned relations like is-mother-of or is-less-than can be discussed as subsets of cross-products of some sets as follows.

2.2.1 Definition, Notation and Illustrations

  • In Mathematics, a relation from a set X to a set Y is defined as a subset of the cross- product X xY.
  • Earlier mentioned relations like is-mother-of or is-less-than can be discussed as subsets of cross-products of some sets as follows.
  • Notation (in Mathematics) If Sheela is the mother of Shivam, then the fact may be expressed as Sheela is- mother-of Shivam.
  • In mathematics, it is preferred to denote the fact as (Sheela, Shivam) ∈ is-mother-of, where the relation “is mother of” is considered as the set of all the pairs (m, c), for which m “is mother” of c.

2.3 Properties of Relations

  • We will discuss properties of only for those relations R for which the domain and range is the same set, say X, i.e., the relations on a set, say X.
  • Unless mentioned otherwise, all relations are on the set X (fixed for all the relations under consideration).
  • The discussion revolves around three important properties of relations on a set, viz.
  • (i) reflexive, (ii) symmetric, and (iii) transitive.

2.4 Equivalence relations, and Partition of a Set

  • PARTITION OF A SET A relation R on a set X is said to be an equivalence relation, if R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
  • In more detailed form, R is an equivalence relation on set X, if and only if (i) R is reflexive on X, i.
  • for every x ∈ X, we have (x, x) ∈R, and (ii) R is symmetric on X, i.
  • for x, y ∈ X, if (x, y)∈ R, then (y, x) ∈ R, and (iii) R is transitive on X, i.

2.5 Partial Order Relation, Partially Ordered Set

  • For an equivalence relation R on a set X, the subset [a] of X defined as [a] = {𝑥∈ X: (x, a) ∈R} is called an equivalence class of a under the equivalence relation R.
  • Example: Consider the relation R= {(a, a), (b.
  • b), (b, c), (c, b), (c, c)} on set X= {a, b, c}.
  • Two equivalence classes in X under R are {a} and {b, c}.

2.5.1 Applications of Equivalence Relation and Partition of a Set

  • Motivation for equivalence relation is that for some specific purpose, many apparently distinct elements behave identically, and hence need not be distinguished from each other.
  • By clubbing all such elements, we reduce complexity for designing solutions of problems concerning the purpose.
  • These 20 class sections determine a partition of the set of all students in the school.
  • The equivalence relation has useful applications in the design of digital computers and other sequential machines.

2.5.2 Partial Order Relation, Partially Ordered Sets

  • A relation R on a set X is said to be a partial order, if R is reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive.
  • In more detailed form, R is an partial order on set X, if and only if i) R is reflexive on X, i.
  • for every x ∈ X, we have (x, x) ∈R, and ii) R is anti-symmetric on X, i.
  • for x, y∈ X, if (x, y)∈ R, and (y, x) ∈ R, then x=y, and iii) R is transitive on X, i.

2.6.1 Set-type Operations on Relations

  • The set-type operations on relations include union of relations, intersection of relations etc.
  • We explain this type of operation on relations only through examples.
  • Mapping-type operations: inverse of operation, composition i) For a relation R from set X to Y, the inverse relation of R, denoted by R-1 is the relation from Y to X, such that (y, x) ∈R-1, if and only if (x, y) ∈R.
  • Here, R and S are defined in a slightly different way than these were defined just above.
